title: A pesar de: in spite of the obstacle

sections.content: You know *a pesar de* + noun or infinitive, *a pesar de que* + a verb, and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32. They introduce an obstacle that did not stop what happened next. Transitions to democracy are full of such obstacles: laws that protected the military, immunity, referendums.

items.spanish: A pesar de esas leyes, muchas organizaciones siguieron pidiendo justicia.
items.english: In spite of those laws, many organisations kept asking for justice.

items.spanish: A pesar de su inmunidad como senador vitalicio, Pinochet fue detenido en Londres.
items.english: In spite of his immunity as a senator for life, Pinochet was arrested in London.

items.spanish: La ley siguió vigente a pesar de que muchas personas la criticaban.
items.english: The law stayed in force although many people criticised it.

items.spanish: Pese a los cambios de gobierno, las familias siguieron pidiendo verdad.
items.english: Despite the changes of government, the families kept asking for the truth.

sections.content: Never drop *de*: *a pesar de*, not *a pesar* alone. Use *a pesar de* before a noun or infinitive (*a pesar de esas leyes*) and *a pesar de que* before a conjugated verb (*a pesar de que la criticaban*). *Pese a* means the same and is a little more formal.
